title: Praggnanandhaa Wins Saint Louis Rapid and Blitz, Surges to Second in Grand Chess Tour
excerpt: The 21-year-old Indian grandmaster dominated the field with 23½ points, finishing 1½ points clear of nearest rival Javokhir Sindarov and climbing within half a point of tour leader Fabiano Caruana.
body:
• R Praggnanandhaa scored 23½ points (12 in rapid, 11½ in blitz) to win the 2026 Saint Louis Rapid and Blitz outright, claiming $50,000 and 13 Grand Chess Tour points.
  • The victory lifts the Indian GM to second place in the overall GCT standings with 24.5 points, just half a point behind leader Fabiano Caruana heading into the final two events.
  • Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov finished second with 22 points, while American Wesley So took third with 20½.
  • Praggnanandhaa had led the tournament from start to finish, taking sole command on day one and never relinquishing his advantage across 27 rounds.

Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa sealed the 2026 Saint Louis Rapid and Blitz title on Wednesday, capping a wire-to-wire performance that vaulted him into contention for the overall Grand Chess Tour championship with two events remaining.

The 21-year-old from Chennai scored 23½ points across the five-day tournament — 12 in the rapid portion and 11½ in blitz — finishing 1½ points clear of Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in a field of ten elite grandmasters at the Saint Louis Chess Club, according to final standings published by the Grand Chess Tour.

Dominant From the First Move

Praggnanandhaa set the tone on day one, scoring five out of a possible six points in rapid to take sole leadership. By the end of day two, he had extended his advantage to two points over Sindarov, as reported by Chess.com. The Indian prodigy maintained that cushion through 18 rounds of blitz, never allowing his rivals to mount a serious challenge.

"Dominant From the First Move Praggnanandhaa set the tone on day one, scoring five out of a possible six points in rapid to take sole leadership."

American veteran Wesley So finished third with 20½ points, while wildcard Levon Aronian — the defending Saint Louis Rapid and Blitz champion — placed fourth with 19 points. Tour leader Fabiano Caruana had a relatively subdued tournament, tying for fifth with 17 points alongside Jorden van Foreest and Leinier Dominguez.

Germany's Vincent Keymer, who entered the event second in the overall standings, managed just 14½ points for ninth place — a result that significantly dented his tour title hopes.

The GCT Title Race Tightens

The outright victory — achieved without a tiebreak playoff — earned Praggnanandhaa the maximum 13 tour points, catapulting him from fifth to second in the overall Grand Chess Tour standings with 24.5 points. He now trails Caruana by just half a point heading into the Sinquefield Cup, a classical tournament that begins August 10 in the same venue.

The top four players after the Sinquefield Cup will qualify for the GCT Finals, scheduled for August 22–27. With Sindarov also climbing to 20.5 points in the standings, the battle for the four finals berths has tightened considerably.

A Remarkable 2026 Season

The Saint Louis triumph is Praggnanandhaa's second Grand Chess Tour event win this year, following his victory at the 2025 Superbet Chess Classic in Romania where he prevailed in blitz playoffs against Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Alireza Firouzja. He also won the 2025 Tata Steel Chess Tournament and the 2026 Norway Chess event, establishing himself as one of the most consistent performers in elite chess.

The tournament was notably missing Alireza Firouzja, who withdrew from the Sinquefield Cup — and consequently the tour — due to a scheduling conflict with the chess tournament at the Esports World Cup. His absence opened the door for Samuel Sevian to enter as a wildcard in the upcoming classical event.

What's Next

The Sinquefield Cup, the tour's penultimate leg, runs August 10–20 in St. Louis. With just 0.5 points separating first and second in the overall standings, and the top four separated by 4.5 points, Praggnanandhaa has a realistic shot at overhauling Caruana for the tour championship — a feat that would cap one of the most impressive seasons by an Indian chess player in the history of the Grand Chess Tour.
